[b]History of Thýven/Sýven: Opening[/b]
The history of the state of Thýven is one as vast and complex as the society itself. From the early days of the Thrømm people when they were a loose collection of tribes dwelling in the forests and hills of southern Elsyr to the present organised state under the 6th dynasty, the nation is steeped in culture and tradition which is uniquely Thrømm and yet diverse. 

Prehistory:
The earliest records of the Thrømm appear nearly 870 years prior to the foundation and unification of the Thrømm in 932 AD under king Þaodex I of Nothmire. The records though sparse in their nature, and relegated to supposition and assumption, are believed to tell of a legendary figure known as Thynag (pronounced Thínog) who lived in the northern mountains with his family and a tribe of Thrømm known as the cliff dwellers . It is believed that Thynag was the first crowned chieftain of the Mountain Thrømm and one of the first to tame the dragon Svynnwyrr (pronounced Svinn-Weer), thus earning him the title of Thynag Dúrkos. Thereby creating the origin of the royal title of Dúrkos or dragon crown.

While the title Dúrkos appears in pre-unification literature, the nature of the title is not yet fully understood, as no archaeological evidence has shown any such monarch or chieftain of the name of Thynag to have existed, with most scholars believing that Thynag is late 12th century invention during the Odersyr Dynastys attempts to legitimize their reign over the Thýven.

Nevertheless despite the lack of evidence of a Thynag Dúrkos ever having existed, archaeologists have found evidence of early Thrømm tribes (in the form of burials, goods stashes, and small ruins) scattered across the northern regions, which seem to suggest a common regional origin for the peoples.

Indeed it is an oddity to most biological anthropologists and historians the evolutionary origins of the Thrømm, primarily due to little evidence of them existing far beyond the borders of modern Thýven, which has led many scientists to surmise that the Thrømm are evolutionary isolates. Indeed the Thrømm are an odd people characterised by their highly deerlike features and lean bipedal bodies, standing at around 5 to 5.5 feet in height. The males of course bear large antlers which are believed to have developed as mating symbols in a distant proto-era. While the females do not bear formal antlers, albeit small rings found on the skulls of females suggest that some early ancestor species did bear antlers on both male and females. 

Nevertheless the ancient Thrømm are little known in regards to their culture or ways of life, beyond being a primarily hunter-gatherer society up until the 6th century, with some tribes seemingly not settling down until as late as the 10th century. It is known that they had an extensive trading tradition as given by findings of velar pine sculptures existing in the plains region. What can be proven however is the existence of a dragon riding tribe which would rise to power in the 8th century eventually uniting the nation.
